text: The Patriots' Week 7 Thursday night loss to the Bears in Chicago—a 30-24 defeat that saw Caleb Williams throw two touchdown passes—has laid bare a critical vulnerability that Mike Vrabel, one of his four pillars of team identity, has repeatedly emphasized: the turnover differential, an area where New England continues to struggle. While Rhamondre Stevenson provided a rare bright spot by reaching a career high in receiving yards and approaching 100 carries for the sixth straight season, the offense was hamstrung from the start by the absence of starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown due to injury, which film review suggests may have contributed to Drake Maye's overall performance issues evident on tape. The loss marked Round 2 against Chicago in what appears to be an ongoing competitive series, and as the Patriots' coaching staff and players offered postgame reflections, the overarching narrative centered on New England's need to shore up ball security and limit defensive mistakes if they hope to turn this season around.
